title: vault-prefs — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::encode_prefs_blob_raw + protocol::decode_prefs_blob. Three case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip success), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure surface per spec §6.4 + §9.5.5). The Rust reference implementation lives at protocol/src/prefs.rs (main myne repository); spec contract is docs/spec/protocol.md §9.5 + §3.4 + §5.2.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'vault-prefs/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin the encoder's byte output

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). The encoder derives prefs_key from this via the canonical derive_subkey helper (SubkeyRole::PrefsKey).

input_account_number_hash_hex.description: 16-byte account_number_hash (hex). Bound into the 39-byte AAD via aad_prefs_blob.

input_plaintext_canonical_utf8_hex.description: Canonical-JSON plaintext bytes (hex). The encoder produces this from the PrefsView via canonical_json_encode; pinning the bytes catches canonical-encoding drift.

input_prefs_nonce_hex.description: 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (hex). Production callers source from OS CSPRNG; vectors pin a constant.

informational_prefs_key_hex.description: 32-byte HKDF output (hex), pre-computed from the root_key. Informational — verified implicitly via the expected_prefs_blob_hex assertion; carried so reviewers don't have to re-derive to inspect intermediate state.

expected_prefs_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output (34-header + ciphertext + 32-CTX-tag), hex-encoded lowercase. Decoders compare byte-equal.

oneOf.title: decrypt_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip

expected_plaintext_canonical_utf8_hex.description: The canonical-JSON re-encode of the decoded PrefsView (hex). For ordinary round-trip cases this equals the sealed inner plaintext; for forward-compat tolerance cases (sealed plaintext carries unknown additive fields, spec §9.5.2) it is the canonical form WITHOUT the unknown fields — the sealed bytes then live in informational_sealed_plaintext_utf8_hex.

informational_sealed_plaintext_utf8_hex.description: Optional. The verbatim inner plaintext that was sealed into input_blob_hex, when it differs from expected_plaintext_canonical_utf8_hex (forward-compat tolerance cases only). Informational — runners decrypt the blob; this field lets reviewers inspect the unknown-field payload without an AEAD implementation.

ai_enabled.description: Local-AI master toggle (SYNC-12, local-ai epic MYND-406). Option<bool>; absent ≡ host-applied default-OFF (opt-in, privacy-default). Only an explicit true/false emits the key. Canonical key 'ai_e' sorts ahead of screen_capture_protection.

ai_excluded_folders.description: Local-AI per-folder exclusion set (SYNC-14, local-ai epic MYND-406). Folder-path strings the AI runtime must never read/embed. Set-canonical: sorted+deduped; omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'ai_ex' sorts after ai_enabled, ahead of screen_capture_protection.

ai_provider.description: The REMOTE AI provider the user named (ai-remote-providers, myne#415, SYNC-15). Closed wire value; omitted when unset, and unset is the default and the UNREACHABLE state rather than a disabled one. The destination URL is NOT carried here — it is a compiled-in client constant, so a tampered blob cannot redirect traffic. Canonical key 'ai_provider' sorts after ai_excluded_folders, ahead of archive_disabled. A decoder MUST treat an unrecognized value as no provider rather than rejecting the blob; this enum pins the set a v0.1 client emits, not the set it must tolerate.

ai_provider_consent.description: WHICH provider the one-time consent was given for (myne#415, SYNC-22). A provider NAME, not a boolean, because consent is per provider: the consent screen names the recipient, so an approval for one cannot stand in for another. A request is permitted only when this equals the active ai_provider — a comparison, rather than an invariant every setter must remember to maintain. Omitted when consent has not been given (the default). It is a GATE, not a display flag: the request path checks it. Device-local — it does NOT sync, so a newly enrolled device inherits the provider, the model and the key but not the approval, and must record its own before a request is permitted (myne-md/myne#456). It was account-scoped and synced until then; the sibling ai_provider_key deliberately still syncs, because rotating or revoking a credential must reach every device. TWO CONSEQUENCES an independent port has to implement and no vector pins: a device-local field is NEVER stamped in field_clocks (protocol.md §9.5.2 ties the two together), so a conformant reader stops stamping this one and IGNORES a pre-existing stamp rather than treating it as an error, since a vault written before the reclassification may carry one. And the not-synced claim is true of a vault only once every client on the account has updated: shared fields get scalar-LWW, so during the rollout window an un-updated client still replicates this field across devices, which is a transition state rather than a defect. Canonical key between ai_provider and ai_provider_key.

ai_provider_key.description: API key for the named remote provider (myne#415, SYNC-15). Present in the ENCRYPTED blob like any other vault content, and MUST NOT cross the host→UI boundary in any implementation — the reference client marks it serde-skip and hands the UI a has-key boolean instead (protocol.md §9.5.2). Omitted when unset. Canonical key 'ai_provider_key' sorts after ai_provider_consent, ahead of ai_provider_model.

ai_provider_model.description: WHICH model at the named provider answers (myne#415, SYNC-24). There is no default and an implementation MUST NOT substitute one — the value comes from the list the provider itself reports, because a client-pinned model tag rots faster than the release that pinned it and on a metered API a default nobody chose is a bill nobody chose. Absent, the remote arm has nothing to ask with and refuses; it never falls back. Unlike ai_provider_key beside it this value DOES cross the host→UI boundary — a published model name is not a credential and the settings surface renders the current selection back. Omitted when unset. Canonical key 'ai_provider_model' sorts after ai_provider_key, ahead of archive_disabled.

device_names.description: MYND-459 / SYNC-41 device friendly-names. BTreeMap<String, String> — device_id-hex -> display name. Omitted-when-empty; members emitted in lexicographic key order. Canonical key 'd' — after deliberate_folders, before editor_*.

archived_folders.description: Folder-archive set (folder-archive). Canonical trailing-slash folder-path strings archived as a UNIT; set-canonical (sorted+deduped), omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'archived_folders' sorts between 'archive_disabled' and 'auto_lock_seconds'.

auto_tag_enabled.description: On-device tag-suggestion toggle (MYND-651). Positive-opt-in bool: default false, emitted ONLY when true — so a vault that never enabled it is byte-identical to a pre-feature vault.prefs (the ai_enabled / cli_enabled convention). Canonical key 'auto_tag_enabled' — after auto_lock_seconds (auto_l < auto_t), before bar_items_order (a < b). It is the second half of a two-key gate: the tag pass runs only when this AND ai_enabled are both on, and the host re-reads both before touching the model.

item_order.description: MYND-183/MYND-596 container-keyed manual sidebar order. BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> — container path ("" ≡ the tree root, or a canonical trailing-slash folder display path) → that container's children in manual order (note UUIDs + full-path child folder paths, freely interleaved, discriminated by the trailing /). Keys NFC-normalized + lexicographically ordered; each value sequence is order-preserved (NOT sorted, NOT deduped). Omitted-when-empty. Retyped from a flat string array by MYND-596 (per-container LWW merge). Canonical key 'item_o' — after item_colors ('item_c'), before keymap ('k').

keymap.description: MYND-304 user keybinding overrides. BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> — command id → set of canonical chord strings (CodeMirror-compatible Mod-Shift-g form, logical key, unresolved cross-platform Mod). Overrides only (defaults live in code); an empty array [] is the explicit-unbind state, distinct from an absent command. Omitted-when-empty (whole field); inner keys emitted in lexicographic order, each chord array set-canonical (NFC + sorted + exact-deduped). Canonical key 'k' — after item_order, before label.

theme.description: MYND-110 user theme preference. Option<ThemeChoice> — absence of the key is the canonical encoding of system (follow the OS); light/dark are the recognized choices. NOT an enum: per protocol.md §9.5.2 the codec ROUND-TRIPS an UNRECOGNIZED string value (a hypothetical future 'sepia'/'amoled') verbatim — the client treats an unknown value as system at apply-time, never a parse failure — so the byte-level vector pins any string (see the decrypt-themed-amoled forward-compat case).

daily_date_format.description: MYND-191 daily-notes date-format string (e.g. YYYY-MM-DD). Option<String>; absent ≡ host-applied default YYYY-MM-DD.

daily_folder.description: MYND-191 daily-notes folder path (canonical trailing-slash). Option<String>; absent ≡ host-applied default Daily/.

daily_template.description: MYND-191 daily-notes template pointer (UUIDv7). Option<String>; absent ≡ blank daily note.

date_format.description: Display date format (myne#279) — one of system / iso / dmy / mdy / dmmmy. Option<String>; absent ≡ system (follow the OS locale), applied host-side. Stored as a free string rather than an enum, with the unknown→default fallback on the client (the editor_content_width precedent) — so like 'theme' the codec round-trips an unrecognized value verbatim rather than rejecting the blob. DISPLAY ONLY: it never enters a .myn file, a blob or the sync wire as a formatting instruction; the on-disk task bytes stay format-free. Canonical key 'date_format' — after daily_template (dai < dat), before deliberate_folders (da < de). Omitted when absent.

field_clocks.description: MYND-478 per-field LWW clocks for the Phase 2 prefs sync (sync-protocol.md §10.2). BTreeMap<String, u64> — a SHARED preference's field name (or a namespaced device_names/<key> per-entry name) → the epoch-MILLISECONDS a setter last changed it. Absent clock counts as 0 to the merge; equal clocks tie-break byte-lexicographically toward the greater value. Omitted-when-empty (every pre-MYND-478 blob); members emitted in lexicographic key order; values bare non-negative integers (floats forbidden). Canonical key 'fi' — after favorites (fa), before folder_icons (fo).

folder_icons.description: MYND-185 per-folder custom sidebar icons. BTreeMap<String, String> — canonical trailing-slash folder path → icon name. Omitted-when-empty; members emitted in lexicographic key order. Canonical key 'f' — after favorites, before item_colors.

item_colors.description: MYND-184 per-item color labels. BTreeMap<String, String> — a heterogeneous note-UUID-or-folder-path key (discriminated by the trailing /) → color-slot name. Omitted-when-empty; members emitted in lexicographic key order. Canonical key 'i' — after folder_icons, before item_order.

label.description: MYND-205 per-vault display name (the in-app vault switcher label). Option<String>; absent ≡ unlabelled (client shows a neutral 'Vault N' fallback). Encrypted-only — lives solely inside vault.prefs. NFC-normalized on encode. Canonical key 'l' — after item_order, before screen_capture_protection.

last_backup_at.description: Unix epoch seconds of the vault's last backup export (MYND-58, vault-backup-restore epic). Absent ≡ never backed up; bare-decimal u64 (floats FORBIDDEN per spec §9.5.2); sorts label < last_backup_at < screen_capture_protection.

paired_at.description: MYND-442 Unix epoch seconds of the in-app pairing-accept time. Additive optional field (§9.5.2) — omitted from the canonical record when absent so pre-feature records stay byte-identical; bare-decimal u64. Per-record canonical key order extension_id < paired_at < revoked < token_value.

paired_extensions.description: MYND-443 browser-clipper paired-extension records (the persisted pairing-token registry). Array of {extension_id, token_value, revoked, paired_at?} sorted by (extension_id, token_value) so the encoding is byte-stable. Omitted-when-empty (the field is absent entirely when no extension is paired). Canonical key 'p' — after last_backup_at, before saved_views/screen_capture_protection.

saved_views.description: MYND-273 Saved Views — array of saved-view definition objects {id, name, view_type, filters (recursive AST), sort, optional card_size/columns/group_by/image/image_aspect_ratio}. The view object's internal shape (incl. the recursive filters AST) is contracted by protocol.md §9.5.2 + the Saved Views feature, not re-modeled here — the codec round-trips it as opaque canonical JSON. Sorted by view id; omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 's' — after paired_extensions, before screen_capture_protection.

view_order.description: MYND-273 Saved Views display order — view ids in render order (sequence semantics: NFC, order preserved verbatim, never sorted/deduped). Omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'v' — sorts last (after theme).

editor_line_numbers.description: editor-line-numbers (MYND-314) optional line-number gutter toggle. Option<bool>; absent ≡ host-applied default-OFF (prose-first). Only an explicit true/false emits the key. Canonical key slot: after editor_layout, before screen_capture_protection (editor_la < editor_line_n < s).

editor_vim_mode.description: vim-keyboard-mode (MYND-313) optional modal (vim) editing toggle. Option<bool>; absent ≡ host-applied default-OFF (modal editing is opt-in). Only an explicit true/false emits the key. Canonical key slot: after editor_toolbar_order, before favorites (editor_to < editor_v < f). Non-load-bearing: a tampered/replayed value can at worst turn modal editing on or off — no clamp. Phase 2 sync classification: device-local (like every other editor_* field), so the local value always survives the merge.

archive_disabled.description: archive-disable optional toggle disabling the note-archive feature's UI entry points. Option<bool>; absent ≡ host-applied default-OFF (archiving enabled). Only an explicit true/false emits the key. Canonical key slot: after active_workspace, before auto_lock_seconds (ac < ar < au).

active_workspace.description: MYND-308 active workspace slot id. Option<String>; absent ≡ host-applied default workspace policy. Free string stored verbatim (NFC-normalized on encode). Canonical key 'active_workspace' — sorts FIRST, before auto_lock_seconds (ac < au).

editor_default_view_mode.description: MYND-299 editor default view-mode preset (live|reading|source). Option<String> stored as a free enum string; absent ≡ host-applied default. Canonical key slot: after editor_content_width, before editor_focus_dim_inactive (editor_c < editor_d < editor_f).

editor_focus_dim_inactive.description: MYND-348 editor focus-mode dim-inactive toggle. Option<bool>; absent ≡ host-applied default focus policy. Only an explicit true/false emits the key. Canonical key slot: after editor_default_view_mode, before editor_focus_typewriter (editor_focus_d < editor_focus_t).

editor_focus_typewriter.description: MYND-348 editor focus-mode typewriter-scrolling toggle. Option<bool>; absent ≡ host-applied default focus policy. Only an explicit true/false emits the key. Canonical key slot: after editor_focus_dim_inactive, before editor_font_family (editor_focus < editor_font: c < n).

right_panel_active_tab.description: Right-panel tabs active-tab pointer. Option<String>; absent means host default (first visible tab). Free string stored verbatim (NFC on encode). Canonical key after paired_extensions, before the hidden-tabs set.

right_panel_hidden_tabs.description: Right-panel tabs hidden set. Vec<String>; set-canonical (NFC+sorted+deduped on encode), omitted-when-empty. Canonical key after the active-tab pointer, before the tab-order sequence.

right_panel_tab_order.description: Right-panel tabs display order. Vec<String>; sequence (verbatim), omitted-when-empty. Canonical key after the hidden-tabs set, before saved_views.

attachment_compression_enabled.description: ingest-image-compression toggle. Inverse-default bool: default true, emitted ONLY when false (like attachment_ocr_enabled). Canonical key 'attachment_c' — before attachment_ocr_enabled.

attachment_ocr_enabled.description: image-OCR toggle (MYND-441). Inverse-default bool: default true, emitted ONLY when false. Canonical key 'attachment_o'.

time_format.description: Display time format (myne#279) — one of system / 24h / 12h. Option<String>; absent ≡ system (follow the OS locale), applied host-side. Same free-string + client-side-validation discipline as date_format. DISPLAY ONLY — never enters a .myn file, a blob or the sync wire. Canonical key 'time_format' — after theme (th < ti), before timezone (_ < z). Omitted when absent.

timezone.description: Display timezone override (myne#279) — an IANA zone identifier; absent ≡ system (the host's own zone). DISPLAY ONLY, and load-bearing for a privacy reason the other two are not: it decides what the app calls 'today' and how a stored wall-clock value is printed, and it NEVER reaches note bytes. Myne emits no timezone offset and no zone identifier into a .myn file — times are local wall-clock — which keeps a coarse geolocation datum out of a file that gets exported as plaintext. Storing the DISPLAY choice in the encrypted vault.prefs does not walk that back. Canonical key 'timezone' — after time_format (_ < z), before transcription_enabled (ti < tr). Omitted when absent.

transcription_enabled.description: speech-to-text toggle (MYND-592). Inverse-default bool: default true, emitted ONLY when false. Canonical key 'transcription_enabled' — after timezone (ti < tr), before view_order.

show_note_timestamps.description: sidebar-note-timestamps toggle. Inverse-default bool: default true, emitted ONLY when false. Canonical key 'show_n' — before show_task_marker.

show_task_marker.description: task-marker toggle (MYND-613). Inverse-default bool: default true, emitted ONLY when false. Canonical key 'show_t'.

reminders_enabled.description: reminders toggle (MYND-618). Inverse-default bool: default true, emitted ONLY when false. Device-local. Canonical key 'reminders_enabled' — after reminder_horizon_days.

reminder_horizon_days.description: reminder horizon in days (MYND-618). Option<int>; bare decimal, omitted-when-unset. Device-local. Canonical key 'reminder_h' — before reminders_enabled.

developer_mode.description: Developer-mode master switch (MYND-593). Positive-opt-in bool: default false, emitted ONLY when true (ai_enabled convention). Canonical key 'developer_mode' — between deliberate_folders and device_names.

cli_enabled.description: CLI terminal-access door (MYND-490). Positive-opt-in bool: default false, emitted ONLY when true. Canonical key 'cli_e' — after bar_items_order, before cli_excluded_folders.

cli_excluded_folders.description: CLI folder-exclusion set (MYND-490). Set-canonical (NFC + sorted + deduped), omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'cli_ex'.

cli_rate_limit_disabled.description: CLI socket rate-limit off switch (MYND-490). Option<bool> (archive_disabled shape); omitted-when-unset. Canonical key 'cli_r'.

color_groups.description: Graph color-group rules (MYND-604). Array of {color, enabled, filter, id, name} objects encoded in caller order VERBATIM (order is rule precedence — never id-sorted, unlike saved_views); the array-grammar itself is pinned by the color-group vector category. Omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'col' — between bar_items_order (via cli_*) and custom_theme.

custom_theme.description: Custom-theme file-stem name (MYND-297). Option<String>, NFC, omitted-when-unset; takes precedence over theme. Canonical key 'cus' — the only 'c'-after-'col' key, between color_groups/cli_* and daily_*.

icon.description: Vault-switcher glyph name (vault-icon). Option<String>, NFC, encrypted-only, omitted-when-unset. Canonical key 'icon' — between hidden_bar_items and item_colors.

bar_items_order.description: Bottom-bar element order (bottom-bar customization). Sequence array (NFC, order preserved verbatim, NOT sorted/deduped), omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'bar_items_order'.

hidden_bar_items.description: Bottom-bar hidden set (bottom-bar customization). Set-canonical (NFC + sorted + deduped), omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'hidden_bar_items'.

editor_content_width.description: editor-typography content-width preset (narrow|normal|wide|full). Option<String> stored verbatim, omitted-when-unset. Canonical key 'editor_c'.

editor_font_family.description: editor-typography font-family preset (mono|sans). Option<String> stored verbatim, omitted-when-unset. Canonical key 'editor_fo' — before editor_layout.

editor_line_spacing.description: editor-typography line-spacing preset (tight|normal|relaxed). Option<String> stored verbatim, omitted-when-unset. Canonical key 'editor_line_s' — after editor_line_numbers.

editor_text_size.description: editor-typography text-size preset (sm|md|lg|xl). Option<String> stored verbatim, omitted-when-unset. Canonical key 'editor_t' — after editor_slash_order, before editor_toolbar_*.

editor_slash_hidden.description: Slash-menu hidden set (MYND-336). Set-canonical (NFC + sorted + deduped), omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'editor_slash_h'.

editor_slash_order.description: Slash-menu display order (MYND-336). Sequence array (order preserved verbatim), omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'editor_slash_o'.

editor_toolbar_hidden.description: Floating-toolbar hidden set (MYND-336). Set-canonical (NFC + sorted + deduped), omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'editor_toolbar_h'.

editor_toolbar_order.description: Floating-toolbar display order (MYND-336). Sequence array (order preserved verbatim), omitted-when-empty. Canonical key 'editor_toolbar_o' — before editor_vim_mode.

spell_enabled.description: Spell-check toggle (MYND-267). Option<bool>, omitted-when-unset. Canonical key 'spell_e' — before spell_languages.

spell_languages.description: Active spell-check BCP-47 language tags (MYND-267). Set-canonical (NFC + sorted + deduped), omitted-when-empty, case-sensitive. Canonical key 'spell_l'.

new_note_location.description: New-note placement mode (MYND-462, root|current|specific). Option<String> stored verbatim, omitted-when-unset. Canonical key 'new_note_location' — between last_backup_at and new_note_location_folder.

new_note_location_folder.description: New-note target folder for the 'specific' mode (MYND-462). Option<String>, canonical trailing-slash, omitted-when-unset. Canonical key 'new_note_location_f'.

startup_open.description: Startup file mode (MYND-462, last|empty|specific). Option<String> stored verbatim, omitted-when-unset, device-local. Canonical key 'startup_open' — between screen_capture_protection and theme.

startup_open_note.description: Startup note UUID for the 'specific' mode (MYND-462). Option<String>, omitted-when-unset, device-local. Canonical key 'startup_open_n'.

expected_prefs_view.description: Parsed PrefsView shape. v0.1.x fields (MYND-160 + MYND-183 + MYND-110 + MYND-205): screen_capture_protection (required bool) + the omitted-when-default optionals deliberate_folders / auto_lock_seconds / editor_layout / favorites / item_order (item_order heterogeneous: note UUIDs + folder paths) / theme (light|dark, absent ≡ system) / label (per-vault display name, absent ≡ unlabelled). The cases-array shape stays additive — new cases, immutable old ones. / last_backup_at (epoch seconds, absent ≡ never backed up, MYND-58)

oneOf.title: decrypt_aead_fail — pin the non-distinguishing failure surface

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST report a non-distinguishing AEAD failure (Rust reference: PrefsBlobError::CannotDecrypt). Implementations MUST NOT distinguish cross-vault vs tampered vs wrong-key beyond the single 'cannot decrypt' outcome.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable structural or inner-plaintext reject

input_blob_hex.description: A malformed blob (hex, empty allowed). Six of the seven rejects fire BEFORE the AEAD stage (magic / protocol_version / reserved / length checks); plaintext_parse_failed fires AFTER a successful AEAD open, on the canonical-JSON parse.

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). REAL key, deliberately: the header bytes are not bound into the AAD, so a port that skips a structural check decrypts the tampered blob successfully and returns Ok — which the runner catches. With a dummy key the same buggy port would report an AEAD failure and pass silently. The plaintext_parse_failed case additionally needs the key to get past AEAD at all.

expected_error.description: The specific reject the decoder MUST surface (Rust reference: PrefsBlobError::{HeaderTooShort, MagicMismatch, ProtocolVersionMismatch, ReservedByteNonZero, CiphertextLenOverflow, CiphertextTruncated, PlaintextParseFailed}). Unlike the AEAD-failure surface (case_kind decrypt_aead_fail), these are intentionally distinguishable for observability — though callers MAY collapse them to PrefsView::default() per §9.5.5.
